findings.description: W1 THE SHIPPED FINDINGS RECORD IS A FROZEN PRE-T105 SNAPSHOT, AND t106's OWN ac4 CROSS-CHECK IS INDEX-STATE COUPLED: IT IS GREEN ON THE BRANCH IT WAS VERIFIED ON AND RED ON MERGED MAIN - MEASURED, NOT INFERRED. Review ran the shipped fences out of the archived cards at HEAD (2ca8288/fc2d5d7): t106 ac3 rc=0 and ac5 rc=0, but ac4 rc=1 with 'the fresh run reports leg 282 pinning docs/issues/closed/t76.md but the record's literal_paths are [docs/issues/t76.md]', and ac1/ac2 rc=1 for the disclosed base-shape reason (post-merge HEAD has no strict pre-upgrade ancestor: HEAD^ 2ca8288 already carries the upgrade; merge-base(main,HEAD) is HEAD itself). A full diff of a fresh auditor run against the shipped record at merged main measures TEN path-membership mismatches (282, 306, 308, 309, 310, 311, 312, 315, 316, 317) and TEN classification drifts (record 'moved' vs fresh 'present'), while the leg SET and the two headline counts stay agreeable (13 legs, pinned_legs=13, broken_pins=0, dirty_b64_legs=0, exit 0). The mechanism is precise: ac4 compares the record's literal_paths - which carry the PINNED (pre-move) form - against paths the fresh run reports, and the fresh run reports the decoded payload's current anchor, which t105 moved to docs/issues/closed/; t105 merged first (d918927) and t106 second (b716ad5), so the record describes the index shape its own ac1 was built to test rather than the merged tree. This is NOT a custody breach: the record blob is 484d096e at both b716ad5 and HEAD, i.e. nobody 'fixed' the staleness by rewriting a closed card's artifact, and the card itself states the dual-shape contract ('it is tested against a pre-t105 index (where it must REPORT the eleven hidden pins) and against a post-t105 index (where broken_pins must be 0)'). It is also not a t104-style trap: t104's own ac4 still passes on merged main because its scan is plaintext-only and therefore still yields exactly {230, 279}. Verdict: warning, because the record's OBSERVATIONS are all true of the index state it names and the only false statement would be a reader who takes 'moved' as a property of today's tree. REMEDY for the next tool card: a findings record that is cross-checked against a live tool run must stamp the index blob it was generated against (the record already names the index PATH but not its blob) and its cross-check fence must compare against that same blob - or the card must state, in the record, that the file is a snapshot of a named index blob and is refreshed only by a named operation. The same class is why t103's matrix rows were re-derived rather than quoted.

W2 THE AMENDMENT PRECEDENT IS SOUND AND SHOULD BE ADOPTED AS A TEMPLATE, NOT AS AN AUTHORITY - POLICY FOR FUTURE INDEX-TOUCHING CARDS. t105 is the first non-orchestrator write to docs/state/merge_test_index.json in project history (operator authorization WAL 1241, THIS card only). Review assessed what made it checkable and found EIGHT properties, all of which are reproducible on any future card and none of which is specific to base64 or to card paths: (1) the authorization is recorded OUTSIDE the card first (a WAL entry naming the card), so the card cannot authorize itself; (2) the card amends ownership IN WRITING and ac1 asserts the amendment sentences as card TEXT, so an amendment nobody can point at REDs; (3) the amended SURFACE is DERIVED by decoding the base index blob at run time and must equal the card's named set, so a card that names a leg the index does not hide (or misses one it does) REDs; (4) the byte boundary is proved per leg - changed-leg set equality against the authorized set, command-only key change, exactly one base64 chunk, plaintext skeleton unchanged, and back-substitution recovering the BASE payload byte-for-byte (which is what actually forbids touching leg 307's historical fingerprint data); (5) metadata is FROZEN and the freeze is DISCLOSED (updated_at deliberately unchanged, asserted by ac3 and by the decision record, because re-dating the orchestrator's file would masquerade as an orchestrator index op); (6) a per-leg decision record carries disposition, anchor symbol, MEASURED liveness and rc before/after, with the liveness RE-MEASURED inside the fence rather than quoted; (7) the authorization EXPIRES at merge and says so; (8) the sibling card carries ZERO index bytes and PROVES it (t106 ac5 hashes the index across three tool runs, ac6 refuses any index path in the delta). Review RECOMMENDS the orchestrator treat t105 as the reference shape and adopt this as policy: a builder write to the index is permitted only where a WAL entry names the card, the card states the amendment in checkable text, and all of (3)-(6) are fenced; anything less stays an orchestrator surgical op (which remains the correct route for leg 230's plaintext re-premise and leg 309's pinned-BASE residue, both of which are single-leg defect classes with no per-leg decision surface to defend). Recorded as a warning because the precedent now EXISTS: a future card could cite t105 as authority, and the only thing standing between that and a smuggled index edit is that the future card must satisfy the same eight properties on its own bytes. The card's own anti-transfer language ('this amendment does not transfer ... expires when this card merges') is present and is what this review checked for.

W3 DISPOSITION VOCABULARY DRIFTS ACROSS THREE SURFACES FOR THE SAME EIGHT LEGS, AND THE PLAN STILL ASSERTS THE MECHANISM THE CARD MEASURED AND REJECTED. docs/plan.md line ~2512 and the survey handoff both state t105's per-leg dispositions are 'read_closed vs byte_hygiene_move' and that the card 'REJECTS guard_correct_semantics for all eleven'; the shipped card's ac4 allows EXACTLY {read_closed, guard_correct_semantics} and the shipped decision record uses guard_correct_semantics for the eight dead-constant legs (306/307/310/311/312/315/316/317) and read_closed for 282/308/309. Measured: the string byte_hygiene_move exists ONLY in docs/plan.md and the survey handoff - it never reached a card, a fence or a record. There is no substantive contradiction (fence and record agree leg-by-leg, and the record's per-leg text describes a hygiene move of a dead constant), so this is a vocabulary warning, not an error - but it is exactly the class that re-opens settled questions: a reader holding the plan reads 'REJECTS guard_correct_semantics for all eleven' against a record that says guard_correct_semantics eight times and concludes the builder disobeyed. The same paragraph of plan.md also still carries the survey/WAL-1236 mechanism ('the other eight are GREEN-but-silently-degraded, because their test -f guards skip the probe'), which t105's Context NAMED as a correction after measuring per leg that no leg of the eleven is skipped by a card-missing guard - the card-path constant is simply never read (0 symbol uses beyond the definition, re-measured inside ac4, which hard-codes the live=[282,308,309] / dead=8 split). The measurement-driven correction is the right call and the fence re-measures rather than quotes; the residue is documentary. REMEDY: treat the archived card and the decision record as authoritative over plan.md for this phase, and in future surveys carry the disposition vocabulary forward verbatim from the fence that will enforce it.

W4 THE AUDITOR'S 'present' CLASSIFICATION IS A WORKING-TREE PROPERTY, NOT A FROZENNESS PROPERTY - AND THE INDEX'S OWN SCHEMA LIMITS THE PHASE'S NUMBERING CONVENTION. Review read the shipped classifier: a pinned path is 'present' if os.path.isfile(pinned) in the current checkout, 'moved' if it resolves under docs/issues/closed/ or docs/issues/groom/, and 'missing_everywhere' otherwise. That is the right semantics for an archival-break audit, and ac3's planted-pin negative control proves the broken class bites (payload-only plant on leg 306/315 -> status=missing_everywhere via=decoded_base64, broken_pins 0->1, exit 0; re-run by t106v independently in a throwaway clone). But it means 'present' asserts only 'resolves today', so a leg pinning a live path is GREEN in the report right up to the moment the card is archived - which is the t104 blindness this phase exists to shrink, now merely narrowed rather than eliminated. Two consequences for policy: any gate that consumes broken_pins must be told that present != safe, and the next archival batch must re-run the auditor BEFORE moving cards, not after. Separately, review measured that 193 of the 318 stored legs carry no 'ac' key at all (only 125 do), so the phase's binding convention - every leg reference carries issue_id AND ac - is satisfiable only for the 125 legs that have one; the auditor prints ac=None for the rest (no leg pinned today is affected: all 13 carry ac). Future index work should not treat a missing ac as an index defect, and leg references for those legs should carry issue_id plus the command's own ac literal where present.

W5 COVERAGE: BOTH OPERATOR-DIRECTED WORKSTREAMS (WAL 1241's '分開開卡' split) ARE COVERED, THE FOUR NON-COVERAGES ARE DELIBERATE AND NAMED, AND THE HIDDEN-PIN CLASS IS MEASURABLY CLOSED OUTSIDE THREE DISCLOSED RESIDUES. Step 1 against docs/requirements.md and docs/plan.md's phase_17 section: neither card introduces or deletes a REQ-ID (each card's text mentions 'NO NEW REQ-ID' exactly once and cites only anchor families its touched surface already carries - t105 the verification-evidence family of the re-premised t76/t86/t87/t88 legs, t106 the t104 checker/hygiene anchors), and docs/requirements.md is frozen by both cards' ac5, so no requirement's verification target moved and no REQ_ROW was added or removed (the archival commit re-ran the generator byte-equal: rows=749 gap=0 unpointed=0, WAL 1247). The non-coverages are recorded, not absorbed: leg 230 (plaintext frozen-RED analogue), leg 279 (t78 live-dir exemption), leg 309's pinned-BASE 67c9db975d75 residue, and the four other criteria documents (scoped out since phase_16). Review re-derived the class independently over all 318 legs (plaintext plus decoded canonical chunks): exactly three legs still name a live docs/issues/tXX.md path - 230 (disclosed non-repair), 279 (disclosed exemption), and 307 (the HISTORICAL npm-audit fingerprint/self-reference forms inside the same payload, which the card names, which ac2's back-substitution forbids editing, and which the t106 record lists as five per-path observations) - so the WAL 1236 class is closed for the eleven legs it was opened for. NO coverage_gap error: the milestone satisfies its directive as written in WAL 1241.

W6 GRANULARITY: BOTH CARDS SIT AT THE AC CEILING, t106's PRODUCT DIFF EXCEEDS THE NOMINAL LINE CEILING, AND THE SURVEY'S GRANULARITY NUMBERS DISAGREE WITH THE CONFIG AGAIN. docs/config.yaml limits.issue_granularity is max_acs=6, max_files=4, max_diff_lines=300, warn_only=true. Both cards carry exactly 6 ACs. Measured product surfaces: t105 = 2 files (docs/state/merge_test_index.json 11/11 lines, docs/state/outputs/t105_repremise_decisions.json 275/0) = 286 diff lines, inside the ceiling; t106 = 2 files (docs/tools/leg_path_pin_audit.py 111/16, docs/state/outputs/t106_checker_b64_findings.json 343/0) = 470 diff lines, over the nominal 300. The survey handoff's granularity_check reported max_files_per_issue=3 / within_limits=true where the config says 4 - the same survey-vs-config mismatch as phase_16 W5, now twice observed. Neither card was split: the operator directed exactly two cards (WAL 1241), each deliverable set is indivisible (one index edit + its decision record; one tool upgrade + its record), and the overage is a machine-generated JSON record's line count, not hand-written scope. The fence bodies themselves (~1100 and ~1018 card lines) are the established t102/t103/t104 evidence-fence shape and are not scope. Accepted under warn_only=true; the actionable item is that survey's granularity_check should read the config rather than restate it.

W7 STEP 4 CLEAN: NO DUPLICATED AND NO CONTRADICTORY AC BETWEEN THE CARDS - THE SHARED ac6 HEADING IS THE PHASE_15 CLOSEOUT RULE, THE BODIES ARE DISJOINT, AND THE MUTUAL FREEZE IS WHAT MAKES THE SPLIT MEANINGFUL. Both cards' ac6 carry the same heading (delta purity against a run-time-derived base plus groom reproducibility) because both implement the same closeout rule (HEAD^ then merge-base(main,HEAD) then merge-base(origin/main,HEAD), printing every candidate, rejection reason and acceptance; WAL excluded from ALLOWED; ac_hash recomputed, never quoted). Review compared the fenced bodies: they differ in CARD/GROOM/BUILDER literals, in DELIVERABLES (t105: the index and its decision record; t106: the auditor and its record), in the frozen-neighbour lists, and t106's adds the two-tier sibling freeze (absent-at-base-and-tree is the legitimate pre-t105 state; present-in-tree-but-absent-at-base means t105's bytes arrived on this branch and REDs). The owned surfaces do not intersect at all (t105: merge_test_index.json + t105_repremise_decisions.json; t106: leg_path_pin_audit.py + t106_checker_b64_findings.json), and each card freezes the other's surface by bytes - so the two ran in parallel from the same base ab1ab5d and merged in either order without touching each other's bytes (t106's merge contributed ZERO index bytes: blob a4e65098 identical at b716ad5 and HEAD). The only genuine cross-card tension review found is the W1 record/index state coupling, which is a sequencing property of the record, not a contradictory AC.

W8 STEP 3 CLEAN: NO CYCLE, NO DANGLING EDGE, NO ORPHAN DEFECT - AND THE PLAN'S ONE STALE WORD IS 'legs'. Against docs/state/dag.json (generated 2026-10-21T10:37:59Z): 107 nodes, 144 edges, cycles=[], zero edges reference a non-existent node, and t105/t106 appear in the topological order with no in- or out-edges - matching both cards' declared depends: [] and both plan lines ('Depends: []'). Ten nodes carry no edge (t72, t73, t74, t96, t97, t101, t103, t104, t105, t106); all ten are root cards from later phases, not orphans, and this review records the count so a future dependency check does not report the roots as a defect. The parallel claim is not merely asserted but was the execution shape: worktrees t105b/t106b cut from ab1ab5d, both builders dispatched together (WAL 1243), merges d918927 then b716ad5 serialized per WAL 1140 - and the fences survived the order they were not written against (t106's sibling freeze accepts either state). One documentary nit: plan.md's numbering paragraph says 'merge_test_index.json's legs array' where the key is 'tests' (both cards write tests[N], and every fence reads ["tests"]); harmless, but the same paragraph is the binding convention statement, so it should name the real key.

W9 DEVIATIONS JUDGED HONESTLY: FIVE, ALL DISCLOSED, ALL ZERO PRODUCT DELTA - AND TWO OF THEM ARE PROCESS RULES THE ORCHESTRATOR HAS ALREADY CLOSED. (a) t105 harness acceptance-report friction x2 (trailing-comma JSON, then report-not-found on re-emit; WAL 1244): the report exists in the artifact, the orchestrator's own independent scope proof is authoritative, and declining a third resume on diminishing returns is the right call - the friction is in the reporting harness, not the product, and both t105 verifiers then re-ran all six fences verbatim rc=0 with a three-way ac_hash match (8eb9bb52). (b) t106v self-applied the 'verified' label on #112 (custody belongs to the orchestrator) - disclosed BY THE VERIFIER in its own handoff, accepted, and not double-applied; the honest reading is that the verifier's mode doc still contains a step the custody rule moved elsewhere, and the fix is to remove or scope that step, not to blame the agent. (c) The orchestrator's WAL 1241 slug naming error (a digit-bearing 'checker_b64' tail violating the survey schema's ^phase_[0-9]+_[a-z_]+$) was corrected at WAL 1242 with ingest commits e0b95e8/1b5664a, the bad slug has zero refs in the committed tree, and the definer measured blast radius and ASKED rather than guessing - the process worked exactly as designed. (d) The groom gate1 gap: the definer's completion check validated the handoff schema but did not run gate1, so t106's non-canonical headings ('## What to build', '## Verification', a nonexistent out-of-scope heading) reached ingest; the resume fixed headings only (docs-only 17+/6-), the ac_hash 8da34a9d did not move, and the orchestrator's new standing procedure (run gate1 before accepting groom) closes the class. This review owns that one: gate1 card-section validation is the definer's completion obligation, and schema validation alone is not completion. (e) t106's findings-record-NEW rather than rewrite-t104 is the CORRECT call and review endorses it: docs/state/outputs/t104_hygiene_findings.json is the cross-checked artifact of t104's own ac4 and is byte-frozen under t104 custody, and it is the reference t106 ac2 measures plaintext byte-stability against - rewriting it would have destroyed the very thing the stability fence compares to, and would have moved a closed card's evidence. The cost is W1's staleness, which is the price of a snapshot and is fixable by stamping the snapshot's index blob.

W10 SWEEP INTERPRETATION STANDS UP, INCLUDING THE NEW RED, WHICH REVIEW CONFIRMED IS UNRELATED BY CONSTRUCTION. Post-merge 318-leg sweep on merged main: GREEN 281 / RED 37 vs the phase_16 baseline 280/38 (WAL 1247). Recovered 1-based {283, 309} = 0-based {282, 308} - exactly the two legs this phase set out to repair (t76-ac4 and t86-ac3, the card-missing hard failures), which is the maximum this card could repair given 309's disclosed residue. 0-based 309 stays RED as disclosed (its card-missing RED is gone; what remains is its own BASE=67c9db975d75 literal against the post-t84 moves - orchestrator index-defect custody per WAL 1240, and the decision record names it inside leg 309's entry, which ac4 requires). 0-based 230 stays RED as the frozen plaintext analogue (byte-identical base-to-HEAD, proved by t105 ac5), and 0-based 279's t78 pin stayed GREEN throughout, so the exemption rule held. The new RED, 1-based 190 = 0-based 189, is t47's uv/alembic leg: review read the stored command and it carries NO card-path pin and no relation to either card's surface (index payload edits and docs/tools), and it re-ran rc=0 in isolation, matching the same leg's earlier RED->GREEN flip between the phase_16 baseline and post-16 sweep - so the transient-env classification is corroborated independently, not just accepted. Net: zero product regressions, and the targeted rc table at merged main (230=1, 279=0, 282=0, 306-308=0, 309=1, 310-312=0, 315-317=0) equals the groom's prediction leg for leg.

W11 MILESTONE BOOKKEEPING AND SCOPE OF THIS REVIEW: Step 6 APPLIED TO ITSELF (the phase_15 W6 / phase_16 W8 precedent, disclosed rather than silently varied), and NOTHING ELSE WAS TOUCHED. docs/state/milestones/phase_17_pin_repremise_checker_decode.json now carries review_plan_status=passed, review_plan_completed_at=2026-10-22T01:50:00Z, review_plan_verdict=PASS_WITH_WARNINGS and review_plan_attempts incremented 0 -> 1. Both cards are already closed [verified] (#111/#112, WAL 1247) and archived under docs/issues/closed/, so this is a post-milestone plan-split review whose corroborating proof is the milestone's own closeout evidence (WAL 1246's exact rc table and WAL 1247's 281/37 sweep). Per this task's order the definer committed these two files as a docs-only commit and PUSHED, the same shape as phase_16's ingest (one git op per cmd.exe call with read-back); no product file, no card, no DAG, no index byte and no platform call was made by this review, and every fence it executed was read-only against the repository.
